chunks: And it is narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Askari (peace be upon him) that he said:
"Whoever visits Ja'far and his father will not suffer from eye ailments, nor will illness befall him, nor will he die while being tested (with trials)."

key_terms.أَبَاهُ: his father (referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir)
key_terms.زَارَ: visited (specifically visiting the shrines of Imams)
key_terms.مُبْتَلًى: tested (with trials that are considered a blessing or sign of faith)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of visiting Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Askari underscores the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt, linking physical healing from eye ailments and disease to spiritual purification. The promise of dying 'mubtan' (tested) reflects the Shia concept of *ibtila* as a means of elevating rank and purifying sins, rather than a sign of divine displeasure. This connects the physical act of *ziyarah* with the metaphysical reality of enduring trials as a path to ultimate success.
